payload.name: Preserve distinct event facts when updating related memories
payload.description: When a later message references an existing memory's subject or object but describes a different time or a new milestone, use during CRUD to choose ADD over UPDATE and preserve the earlier memory's unique facts.
content: During UPDATE, compare timestamps: if the new message describes a later event related to an existing memory rather than the same occurrence, ADD a new memory for the new event and do not overwrite the existing memory's earlier facts.

If the new event is a later stage of the same project/object, preserve original details (date, ordinal qualifiers like first) in the existing memory; record new state/event separately unless evidence explicitly contradicts the earlier facts.
Do not let emotional or qualitative descriptions from a later message replace concrete factual details from an earlier message; if the earlier facts are not contradicted, keep them.

solves: The diagnosed failure is an UPDATE that overwrote an earlier distinct event (finishing a first screenplay on a known date) with a later related event (the work being shown later), destroying a claim needed to answer a temporal question. The abstract mechanism is conflating related but temporally distinct events during memory maintenance. This rule applies whenever a later message references an existing memory's subject or object but describes a different time or adds new milestones; future construction should preserve earlier unique facts and record the new event separately.
